curation.lead:
Gregory Barbaccia was appointed Federal Chief Information Officer and Federal Chief AI Officer at the Office of Management and Budget on January 27, 2025, as part of the DOGE-associated wave of technology industry placements into senior government roles [Finding #5803]. He is a 10-year Palantir Technologies veteran (2010–2020), where he rose from government account manager to head of the Intelligence and Investigations unit, and a former U.S. Army intelligence sergeant [Finding #6445]. Prior to his appointment he served as Chief Information Security Officer at Theorem Partners and held an advisory board seat at Demand Signal Venture Partners, a defense-technology venture capital firm [Finding #5740].

As Federal CIO, Barbaccia oversees the federal government's approximately $70 billion annual IT budget and sets government-wide IT procurement policy under the Federal IT Acquisition Reform Act [Finding #5952]. In early 2025 he was additionally named Acting Director of the Technology Transformation Services at the General Services Administration—a dual appointment that gave him simultaneous authority over IT policy at OMB and technology acquisition services at GSA [Finding #5965]. His OGE Form 278 financial disclosure filed upon appointment showed retained holdings in Palantir Technologies stock ($1,000–$15,000), a venture-capital position in Anduril Industries through the MWSI fund ($50,000–$100,000, subsequently reported at $100,000–$250,000), and stock positions in Lockheed Martin, Boeing, BAE Systems, Rheinmetall, and ServiceNow—all companies with active or prospective federal IT and defense contracts [Finding #5735] [Finding #5737] [Finding #5742]. The Anduril position was divested by March 2025 per an OMB statement, while the Palantir stock was retained [Finding #5100].

Barbaccia's appointment is one of several concurrent Palantir-to-government placements documented in this investigation. Clark Minor, another Palantir alumnus, was simultaneously installed as HHS CIO, and DOGE-affiliated reporting placed Barbaccia among operatives conducting interviews of career civil servants following the inauguration [Finding #5546]. POGO's Gold Rush investigation named him among administration officials with defense industry financial ties; the Revolving Door Project independently flagged him as a DOGE agent [Finding #5100]. A Periodic Transaction Report (Form 278-T) filed July 1, 2025 indicates active stock trading across 143 disclosed assets during his time in office [Finding #5775].

sections.title: Government Role and Authority
sections.content:
Barbaccia was named Federal CIO on January 27, 2025, with concurrent designation as Federal Chief AI Officer at OMB [Finding #5803]. The Federal CIO role carries authority under FITARA—the Federal IT Acquisition Reform Act—to review and approve major IT investments across all executive branch agencies [Finding #5952]. His stated 2026 priorities are workforce pipeline development, procurement reform, and infrastructure security; Federal News Network reporting identified these as his organizing framework for the $70 billion-plus portfolio he oversees [Finding #5952].

Shortly after his OMB appointment, Barbaccia was additionally designated Acting Director of Technology Transformation Services at the General Services Administration and Senior Advisor to the GSA Administrator—replacing Thomas Shedd, a former Tesla engineer who had initially held the TTS role under DOGE [Finding #5965]. This dual appointment concentrated authority over both the policy layer (OMB/FITARA) and the delivery layer (GSA/TTS) of federal technology acquisitions in a single official who retained financial interests in companies competing for those contracts [Finding #5952]. FedScoop reported the TTS transition; Nextgov covered the original OMB appointment [Finding #5965].

Barbaccia's most recent government experience before this role, according to available reporting, dated to 2009—a gap of roughly 15 years during which he worked in the private defense-technology sector [Finding #5803]. His Association of Former Intelligence Officers membership dates to September 2008, and his ASIS International membership began September 2024, indicating ongoing engagement with the intelligence and security professional community throughout the private-sector interval [Finding #5740].

sections.title: The Palantir Network in Federal Government
sections.content:
Barbaccia's decade at Palantir Technologies (2010–2020) positions him as the most senior Palantir alumnus in the federal government as of early 2025 [Finding #6445]. Palantir held approximately $2.31 billion in all-time Department of Defense obligations and $1.02 billion in FY2025 federal contracts across all agencies at the time of his appointment—a portfolio directly subject to FITARA review authority that his role carries [Finding #6445]. The company's government business model depends on multi-year enterprise agreements and blanket purchase arrangements of precisely the type that OMB's IT procurement policy governs.

Clark Minor, a 13-year Palantir Global Head of Cloud, was simultaneously installed as HHS CIO in May 2025—overseeing the department's $300 million-plus Palantir contract portfolio and the Medicaid data infrastructure that feeds Palantir's ELITE targeting system [Finding #5803, Connection #3260]. The concurrent placement of two senior Palantir veterans at the two agencies with the largest Palantir contract footprints—OMB (policy authority) and HHS (data and health contracts)—is documented in FedScoop reporting on Palantir's agency penetration [Connection #3260].

Within the OMB CIO office itself, DOGE-tracker reporting and ProPublica disclosures identify Allan Mangaser as Senior Adviser to the CIO—also a Palantir and Theorem Partners alumnus, co-located with Barbaccia in the same office [Connection #3280]. A separate concentration exists at OMB's budget function: Thomas Williams, OMB's defense budget director, disclosed spousal Palantir stock holdings of $2 million–$10 million; he was named alongside Barbaccia in POGO's Gold Rush report on Silicon Valley financial ties among administration officials [Connection #3282].

The cross-agency dimension extends to Treasury: Sam Corcos, a DOGE-placed Treasury CIO, oversees the IRS's Palantir contract from that agency's side while Barbaccia's FITARA authority covers the policy framework that governs it [Connection #3283]. Peter Thiel, Palantir's co-founder and a major political donor to members of the current administration, sits at the originating node of this network [Connection #3079, secondHop data].

sections.title: Financial Disclosures and Holdings
sections.content:
Barbaccia's OGE Form 278 filed upon appointment disclosed 143 total assets across four filing documents [Finding #5775]. The core conflict-relevant holdings at time of filing were: Palantir Technologies Class A Common Stock ($1,000–$15,000); an MWSI venture capital fund position in Anduril Industries initially valued at $50,000–$100,000 and reported elsewhere at $100,000–$250,000 [Finding #5100] [Finding #5735]. An OMB statement confirmed the Anduril position was divested by March 2025; the Palantir stock was retained [Finding #5100].

Additional disclosed holdings with federal contract relevance include: Lockheed Martin Corp (LMT, $1,000–$15,000); Boeing Co (BA, $1,000–$15,000); BAE Systems (BAESY, $1,000–$15,000); Rheinmetall ADR (RNMBY, $1,000–$15,000); ServiceNow (NOW, $1,000–$15,000); and Salesforce (CRM, $1,000–$15,000) [Finding #5737] [Finding #5742]. ServiceNow and Salesforce both hold enterprise agreements with federal agencies. Lockheed, Boeing, BAE, and Rheinmetall are defense prime contractors whose IT system integrations intersect with federal CIO policy decisions on architecture standards and interoperability.

The real estate portfolio disclosed includes a Vienna, Virginia property ($250,000–$500,000); an Oakton, Virginia property ($5,000,000–$25,000,000); a Margaretville, New York short-term rental ($5,000,000–$25,000,000); and a Techvestor TVR 2 LLC partnership interest ($100,000–$250,000 with dividend income) [Finding #5742]. His Theorem Partners 401(k) is reported in the $100,000,000–$250,000,000 category—a range that would place its value far above typical CISO compensation, though 278 disclosures use broad bands that may reflect aggregated retirement account totals rather than individual account balances [Finding #5737]. His disclosed net worth is $1,500,000–$4,500,000 [Finding #5965].

A Form 278-T Periodic Transaction Report filed July 1, 2025 documents active stock trading while in office—purchases and sales of multiple holdings—indicating that portfolio activity continued during his tenure overseeing federal IT procurement decisions [Finding #5775]. The source is ProPublica's OGE disclosure database, slug barbaccia-gregory-j, document ID 194 [Finding #5735].

sections.title: Career Background and Pre-Government Record
sections.content:
Before his Palantir tenure, Barbaccia served as a U.S. Army intelligence sergeant and intelligence community analyst, a background consistent with his subsequent role at Palantir managing government accounts in the intelligence and law enforcement sectors [Finding #5803]. His Palantir tenure (2010–2020) moved from government account manager into security leadership and ultimately to head of the Intelligence and Investigations business unit—the division responsible for Palantir's relationships with federal intelligence agencies and law enforcement [Finding #6445].

After leaving Palantir in 2020, Barbaccia served as Head of Core Operations at Theorem Partners from January 2022 through December 2024, and concurrently as an Advisory Board member at Demand Signal Venture Partners—a defense-technology focused VC—from September 2022 through February 2025 (resigning approximately one month after his government appointment) [Finding #5740]. He was also advisory board member at Pagaya, a fintech firm, in January 2025 only, suggesting a rapid wind-down of private commitments upon appointment [Finding #5740]. He founded and remains listed as President/CEO of Launch XYZ LLC, formed September 2024 [Finding #5740].

His membership in the Association of Former Intelligence Officers since September 2008 and in ASIS International since September 2024 places him in the professional networks that bridge the intelligence community with the private defense-technology sector—the same pipeline through which Palantir built its government business [Finding #5740].

What specific IT contracts, procurement approvals, or FITARA compliance reviews did Barbaccia participate in during the period when he retained the Anduril venture position, and were any of those decisions related to Anduril or Palantir?

The Form 278-T filed July 2025 indicates active trading while in office—what specific securities were purchased or sold, and do any of those transactions correspond in timing to procurement decisions or policy announcements affecting those issuers?
What is the scope and purpose of Launch XYZ LLC, which Barbaccia founded in September 2024—three months before his government appointment—and which remained listed as active in his disclosure?

How did the concurrent placement of Barbaccia (Federal CIO, OMB), Allan Mangaser (Senior Adviser to CIO, OMB), and Clark Minor (HHS CIO) come about—were these coordinated through DOGE, through Palantir, or through independent recruitment?
